publications.title: Can Language Models Learn Forever? Stationarity and Plasticity Under Continual Pretraining
publications.tldr: We study when a long-trained language model is still worth continuing on new data, separating how well it holds onto its source corpus (stationarity) from how readily it can still learn (plasticity), and find that weight decay decides whether age slows learning down or speeds it up.

publications.title: Inference on Ceilings: Chandelier Debiasing for Optimal Policy Value with Continuous Treatments under Preference Data
publications.tldr: We develop principled pointwise uncertainty quantification for rewards learned from preference comparisons under a Bradley–Terry model, with a Green-function debiasing correction whose estimator provably attains oracle rates and asymptotic normality.

publications.title: ReflectAgents: Teaching Multimodal Agents to Say No
publications.tldr: We study when reflection is worth its cost for tool-using vision–language agents, defining its value against a matched-compute continuation and using that value to train agents that reflect only when it helps.

publications.title: When Should an Agent Refresh? Adaptive Index Reuse for Efficient Long-Horizon Agentic Reasoning
publications.tldr: Building on IndexCache’s cross-layer index reuse for sparse-attention models such as GLM, we introduce AIR (Adaptive Index Reuse), which uses reinforcement learning to decide when a long-horizon language agent should refresh its sparse-attention selections, improving both success and speed at the same compute budget on coding, terminal and tool-use benchmarks.

publications.title: AIChipBench: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Automated AI Accelerator Design
publications.tldr: We introduce AIChipBench, a benchmark that tests whether LLM coding agents can turn model specifications into working AI accelerator designs, with independent held-out checks that catch failures public tests miss.

publications.title: TAME: Transfer-Aware Model-Harness Co-Evolution through Learned Harness Revisions
publications.tldr: We show that the harness that helps an agent most during training does not always leave the strongest model, and introduce TAME, which trains a feedback agent with reinforcement learning to revise the training harness for gains that transfer to independent deployment harnesses.

publications.title: Verified Experience and Shared Skills for Safe, Speedy, Self-Evolving Coding Agents
publications.tldr: We present S-Code, an open-source coding harness whose self-evolution layer turns observed repairs into short, auditable lessons that later sessions and other agents can safely reuse, without changing model weights or agent code.

publications.title: Physics of Coding Agents: Fit, Not Format at the Edit Interface
publications.tldr: We show that a coding agent’s edit interface works best when it asks for the forms a model writes most reliably: task success hides large differences in cost and failure modes across interfaces, which motivates Verified Selection, a new edit interface built on this fit.

publications.title: Learning Where to Constrain: Meta-Learned Trust Allocation for LLM RL Reasoning
publications.venue: Math Reasoning and AI Workshop, NeurIPS 2026
publications.tldr: We introduce Meta-TA, which meta-learns where an RL trust region should constrain an LLM’s token-level updates during reasoning, replacing hand-set allocations with one learned from feedback.

publications.title: Solving Reflected Diffusion Models: A Physics-Informed Approach
publications.tldr: We build a physics-informed score estimator for reflected diffusion models with a provable dimension-free, uniform-in-time error bound, and show that enforcing the Fokker–Planck boundary condition gives competitive likelihoods and efficient sampling.

publications.title: Phases of Muon: When Muon Eclipses SignSGD
publications.tldr: We provably characterize the high-dimensional training dynamics of stochastic Muon and SignSGD, deriving explicit deterministic dynamics and a phase diagram of when each optimizer wins, which shows why replacing Adam with Muon is not trivial even from a pure optimization perspective.

publications.title: SS-ESOAP: Self-Scaled Adaptive Preconditioning for Physics-Informed Learning
publications.tldr: We introduce SS-ESOAP, a principled self-scaled Kronecker-factored preconditioner for physics-informed neural networks whose scaling factor provably solves a secant-matching problem, reaching lower residuals than first-order and SOAP-style optimizers on most PDE benchmarks.

publications.title: High-Dimensional Isotropic Scaling Dynamics of Muon and SGD
publications.venue: Optimization for Machine Learning Workshop, NeurIPS 2025
publications.tldr: We derive exact risk recursions for Muon and SGD in high-dimensional matrix linear regression, giving principled rules for scaling batch size with dimension and suggesting that Muon’s default normalization may not preserve its nonlinear behavior at scale.

publications.title: Langevin Soft Actor-Critic: Efficient Exploration through Uncertainty-Driven Critic Learning
publications.tldr: We introduce LSAC, an actor-critic algorithm that explores through the uncertainty of a distributional critic learned with Langevin Monte Carlo, aided by parallel tempering and diffusion-generated actions, bringing Thompson-sampling-style exploration to continuous control.
